evals.prompt: How do I serialize a PowerShell object to XML string without writing to a file in PowerShell 7.5?
evals.expected_output: Uses ConvertTo-CliXml / ConvertFrom-CliXml. Shows object -> XML string -> restored object round-trip. Explains difference from Export/Import-Clixml (file I/O vs string). Mentions clipboard use case.

evals.prompt: I want to find all log files older than 30 days in PowerShell 7.5.
evals.expected_output: Uses Test-Path -OlderThan with (Get-Date).AddDays(-30). Shows combining with Get-ChildItem for cleanup. Mentions -NewerThan counterpart.

evals.prompt: How do I download a file and check the status code in one step with PowerShell 7.5?
evals.expected_output: Uses Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile -PassThru. Shows accessing $response.StatusCode and $response.RawContentLength. Explains this eliminates needing a second Get-Item call.

evals.prompt: I'm upgrading from PowerShell 7.4 to 7.5. Will my existing scripts break?
evals.expected_output: States that PowerShell 7.5 maintains backward compatibility with 7.0-7.4 scripts. New parameters are opt-in. No breaking changes to existing cmdlets. Module compatibility preserved.

evals.prompt: Is PowerShell 7.6 still in preview? I heard the += operator got a 16x speedup in 7.6.
evals.expected_output: Corrects both claims. 7.6 is GA/stable (current 7.6.5, .NET 10, LTS; 7.5.10 is the standard 7.5 line). The += array-append optimization landed in 7.5, not 7.6 (measured ~20x vs 7.4; 7.6 is flat vs 7.5). Directs to references/powershell-7.6-features.md for the version table and measured benchmark table.

evals.prompt: What is actually new in PowerShell 7.6? And do I need ConvertFrom-Json -IgnoreComments for JSON with comments?
evals.expected_output: Lists the 7.6-only features verified in the skill: Get-Clipboard -Delimiter and Get-Command -ExcludeModule. States that -IgnoreComments/-AllowTrailingCommas do NOT exist on ConvertFrom-Json/Test-Json; relaxed JSON is Test-Json -Options IgnoreComments/AllowTrailingCommas and ConvertFrom-Json -DateKind, both 7.5+. Also covers the bundled-not-invented DSC v3 and experimental-feature facts as relevant.
